recommended_approach: Cloth with Wind on a subdivided 2D flag mesh, using a pinned hoist-edge vertex group along the pole side
warnings: Low subdivision gives stiff, blocky cloth; the cloth examples recommend subdividing several times (about 8) for floppy fabric.
Use a mesh-based 2D cloth object for fabric; the cloth introduction describes cloth as commonly simulated on a 2D mesh.
For flag setups, pin the pole edge; the examples explicitly describe defining the flag as a grid and pinning the pole edge.
Use smoothing/subdivision after the simulation if the cloth surface looks blocky.
The API lookup did not return usable cloth-specific bpy.types/bpy.ops references in this search pass.
alternative_approaches: Cloth with Animated Vertex Groups for extra art direction over the hoist area or timing.
Cloth on Armature if you need directed large-scale shaping before or during the simulation.
Using Simulation to Shape/Sculpt a Mesh to pre-form a dramatic extended pose, then apply the Cloth modifier.
